description:
FILED s397 (Fable review of s396, `docs/fable-answers-s396.md` §5) — found by
the review's fresh probes, occurs in NO population (perl-tests / t/ / board /
Pl/t), so it is a filler.  Residue of #325.

perlref §"Assigning to References" lists the parenthesized-ARRAY spellings as
lvalues:

    \(@x) = \(@y);              # @x and @y now have the same elements
    \my(@x) = \(@y);            # likewise
    \(my @x) = \(@y);           # likewise
    \(@x) = (\$x, \$y, \$z);    # @x now contains $x, $y, and $z

i.e. the parenthesized array on the LEFT is "the list of @x's element slots,
extended (or truncated) to the right-hand length", each slot aliased to the
corresponding right-hand referent.  (`\(%hash) = …` is FORBIDDEN by perl —
"Can't modify reference to parenthesized hash in list assignment" — and
`\local(@a) = …` too.)

PROBED s397 vs perl 5.40.3 (files in the s397 scratchpad, p8/q1/q4):

    my @a; my ($x,$y)=(1,2); \(@a) = (\$x,\$y); $x=10; print "@a"
        perl: 10 2                PCL: (empty line), exit 0     SILENT WRONG
    my @a=(7,8,9); \(@a) = (\$x,\$y); print scalar @a
        perl: 2  (contents REPLACED, not merged)
    my @y=(1,2,3); \my(@x) = \(@y); $y[0]=9; print "@x"
        perl: 9 2 3               PCL: (empty)                  SILENT WRONG
    my ($x,$y)=(1,2); \(my @c) = (\$x,\$y); $x=10; print "@c"
        perl: 10 2                PCL: (empty)                  SILENT WRONG

The SLICE spellings are already loud (rule 12 die at macroexpansion, correct):
    \@a[5..7] = (\$p,\$q,\$r)   -> "PCL: refaliasing target not supported: (p-list-scalar (p-aslice @a (p-.. 5 7)))"
    \@h{'foo','bar'} = (\$p,\$q) -> same die

CAUSE: the emitter lowers `\(@a) = RHS` as
    (p-setf (p-list-scalar (p-refgen-list @a)) (progn (p-backslash $x) (p-backslash $y)))
— the LEFT is the RVALUE form of `\(@a)` (a list of fresh refs, then p-list-scalar
takes the last one), which is not a `\`-cast place, so p-setf's alias arm
(%p-alias-place-p) does not see it and the write lands in a throwaway box.

FIX SHAPE (CLAUDE.md 11 — one mechanism):
  1. In gen_binary_op_form's `=` lowering, recognise the LEFT shape "refgen over
     a parenthesized list whose single term is a whole ARRAY (incl. `my @x`)"
     — the sibling of _is_backslash_paren_lvalue, which already recognises the
     one-scalar case — and emit `(p-setf (p-backslash-list @a) RHS)` (or route
     it as a new place kind through the same alias arm), never the rvalue form.
  2. Runtime: one helper `p-alias-array-elements (vec refs)`: flatten RHS to
     the referent BOXES via p-alias-scalar-target (so ref-to-ref and
     variable-holding-the-ref stay right — same helper as the scalar arm),
     then REPLACE the vector's contents with those boxes (perl replaces; the
     7,8,9 probe above).  Length = right-hand length.
  3. Rule 12: any OTHER `(p-list-scalar (p-refgen-list …))` place still dies
     naming the target (it does today via the fall-through? NO — today it is
     silent; make the emitter refuse-or-die for the shapes it does not lower,
     so the silent write can never recur).
  4. Guard rows in Pl/t/refaliasing-01.t (probe each expectation vs perl
     first): the four shapes above + INVERSE `\(@a)` in RVALUE position stays a
     list of refs (`my @r = \(@a)` gives N scalar refs — unchanged) + the
     forbidden `\(%h) = …` dies.
BAR: corpus-diff (expect identical — shape absent from every population),
gate, and because cl/pcl-runtime.lisp changes, the full sweep (s377 rule).
subject: refaliasing: the parenthesized-ARRAY spellings `\(@a) = LIST` / `\my(@x)` / `\(my @x)` are SILENT WRONG (rvalue form used as the place)
